exact_statement: Determine how large n must be as a function of r >= 2 so that there is an antichain in 2^[n] occupying n-3 distinct ranks and containing at least r members on every occupied rank.
scope_notes: Round eight proves every actual odd K4,r9 member has a finite recovery rank, while round four proves these ranks have no uniform finite upper bound.
This round asks for an explicit member-dependent upper bound in the odd strip index j, equivalently a log-log bound in q_j or h_j.
A valid bound must follow from all-rank inequalities and the first-wall theorem, not interpolation of computed recovery profiles.

A j-dependent fixed-family bound is a scoped decisive lemma only. It does not imply recovery by rank 42, cover all adjacent orbits, supply suffix persistence, or change the public Erdos-776 threshold.
